info.name: MedAppoint - Appointment reschedule end to end
info.description:
Import this Collection v2.1 JSON and run the ENTIRE collection in order with the Collection Runner (one iteration, no stop-on-failure). Configure environment variables baseUrl (backend origin, no /api), username (email) and password. No IDs, token, dates or valid slots need manual input. Optional startDays=7, searchDays=30, invalidTime=25:99. Environment template: appointments.environment.json. Do not run folders in isolation.

Flow: login -> patient identity -> existing bookings -> active doctor detail -> slot catalog -> create a unique marked appointment -> discover ID -> original detail -> reschedule -> independent detail and list verification -> edge cases -> discover/recheck/delete all marked bookings -> verify deletion -> deleted-ID boundary -> logout.

Every request includes response tests. Contract assertions use actual snake_case API fields; login only requires the documented token. One focused original-detail test checks the YYYY-MM-DD date contract; other steps compare date semantics without repeating that failure. Known F-15 UTC-midnight serialization is normalized ONLY for semantic comparisons; the contract test still fails. Missing-field assertions follow Swagger; past-date, invalid-time and conflict rejection expectations are explicitly proposed rules, not documented guarantees. Failed edge-case persistence is reported and the next scenario uses the latest observed state to avoid cascading false failures. State is checked through independent API GETs, not direct SQL.

This run creates at most two temporary appointments with a unique qa-postman marker, changes only the main appointment, and deletes both. It does not modify pre-existing appointments. Tokens and derived IDs live in run-local variables. Cookies are disabled. Failed prerequisites route to cleanup once a patient is known. Network interruption, manual abort or expired authorization can prevent cleanup; a failed cleanup assertion identifies this. No automated retry creates extra appointments.

Availability limitation: /doctors/{id}/availability exposes only time_slots, and /appointments lists only this patient's appointments. The runner avoids owned bookings and generates distinct future dates in UTC; it cannot guarantee global occupancy or reserve a slot. No second account is supplied, so cross-patient authorization testing is outside this collection.

Postman runner documentation: https://learning.postman.com/docs/tests-and-scripts/running-collections/building-workflows

Scope rationale: one missing-field case represents required-input validation. Past dates, impossible clocks, authentication, occupied slots and deleted IDs exercise distinct risks. Error-body assertions run only after the expected rejection, so a successful invalid write is reported by its status and independent state check rather than three redundant errors.
